The objectives of the literature review were to summarize current, commercial, fossil-based NH production 3 facilities by location, fuel, technology, and scale; survey market prices for commodity NH ; 3 identify end uses for NH , both current uses and future uses for a low-carbon economy; and find 3 contemporary references for NH production flowsheets and process data, including advanced 3 and renewable routes. There are many projects on future U.S. ammonia production; however, this review is focused on recent market and near-term reported projects. 7 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION 1.2 MARKET OVERVIEW Global ammonia production has exhibited steady growth since 2000, driven primarily by increased demand for fertilizers in developing economies and reaching 150 MM tonnes by the present day (Apodaca, 2025). Exhibit 1-1 shows global annual ammonia production over time by country. China produces the most ammonia of any individual country and has grown its annual ammonia production by over 16 MM tonnes over the last 24 years, reaching 42 MM tonnes/year in 2022, which is 28 percent of the world total (Apodaca, 2025). The next three highest-producing countries include the United States, Russia, and India. U.S. ammonia production is on par with Russia and India and has been on the rise in the years preceding 2021. The “Other Countries” category shown in Exhibit 1-1 includes countries that produced on average less than 3 MM tonnes/year such as Saudi Arabia, Iran, Egypt, Germany, France, Pakistan, and Qatar (Apodaca, 2025). Exhibit 1-1. Global ammonia production for 2000–2024 Exhibit 1-2 shows ammonia production capacity and the number of ammonia plants in the United States over time. In 2008, the total number of U.S. ammonia plants fell to a low of 22, with annual ammonia production dropping to a low of 7.7 MM tonnes the following year (Apodaca, 2025). Since then, ammonia production has increased over time, reaching a high of 14.0 MM tonnes/year in 2023, with the total ammonia plants remaining around 35 (Apodaca, 2025), including both coal- and natural gas-based plants. 8 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION Exhibit 1-2. Ammonia production in the U.S. for 2000–2024 The dominant ammonia production technology in the United States is natural gas reforming, accounting for approximately 92 percent of total capacity (EIA, 2021). Exhibit 1-3 shows the number of natural gas-based ammonia plants located in each state. As of 2022, there are 29 natural gas-based plants, operated by 17 companies, and within 16 states (Fernandez, 2024). Iowa, Oklahoma, and Louisiana host the largest number of ammonia plants, at four plants per state (Fernandez, 2024). Exhibit 1-3.
